scenarios.source: The two sections added on 2026-08-14 that the six-step process never had: what the prototype must verify and what would kill the concept, and what is faked in it. Plus the skill's own boundary — a brief that prescribes layout is a specification, not a brief. Plus the fourth intake question added on 2026-08-18: how many directions, because Claude Design otherwise draws the first idea it likes and every later message only polishes that one.
scenarios.why_this_scenario: The request contains its own layout, which means the person does not need a designer, and it plans no validation, which means the prototype will be read as a decision at that meeting. Both failures are quiet: the brief still looks complete.
must: Says that prescribing a modal with three tiles makes this a specification and points at the dev-spec route if the layout really is decided
Writes what the prototype is meant to verify and a kill condition, before anything is shown
Pushes back on the product meeting as the only audience and gets names and a date for someone outside the room
Records the invented data in the „Co je v prototypu nafejkované" section
Gets the rejected competitor patterns named individually, with the reason, instead of a general „nedělej to jako oni"
Names Mini*S as the design system and does not describe visual rules
Outputs the brief as one copyable block and offers it for correction rather than declaring it done
Asks how many directions are wanted — one finished concept or two to three different ones — and writes the answer into the brief with what should differ between them
must_not: Writes layout instructions into the brief
Produces a brief with no kill condition and no audience outside the meeting
Leaves the faked data undocumented because the person said it does not matter
Splits the brief across several messages
Describes colours, spacing or components instead of naming the design system
Writes a brief that leaves the number of directions unsaid, so the designer picks it
scenarios.qualitative: The person thinks they are one message away from a prototype. Does the brief they get back make the meeting safer for them, or does it just add sections?
